visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 mostly maintains a correct ray diagram with the object 30 cm left of the lens, focal point at 10 cm, and a real inverted half-size image 15 cm to the right, whereas Lesson 1 gives the correct formulas but never accurately reveals the final image position/orientation and even shows an upward arrow while discussing negative magnification.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 2 includes a functional, well-formed quiz gate wired after act_equation with a real question, plausible options, a correct answer, and remediation, whereas Lesson 1 has no available gate specs or plan and therefore no evidence of any functioning checkpoint.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 2 has clear, naturally spoken narration with no raw LaTeX defects and only minor repetition, whereas Lesson 1 has no available narration transcript and therefore provides no assessable audio quality.

sync.rationale: Lesson 2 has mostly timed cues that coincide with the relevant narration, despite a few early/late offsets such as revealImage and focusImageDistance, whereas Lesson 1 provides no transcript or cue timing at all and therefore shows no evidence of synchronized visuals.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 correctly derives d_i=15 cm and m=-0.5 while clearly connecting the ray diagram, sign convention, and magnification meaning, whereas Lesson 1 has no transcript or lesson content available to verify accuracy or pedagogical clarity.

polish.rationale: Lesson 2 has a more cohesive modern layout with consistent typography, cards, and readable equations, while Lesson 1 feels sparse and unbalanced with small serif bullet text, large empty areas, and less polished composition despite being visually simple.

aggregator.explanation: All six dimension agents preferred Lesson 2, with generally high confidence. Lesson 2 was judged more visually accurate, with a correct ray diagram and final image representation; substantially more interactive due to a functioning quiz gate; stronger in narration quality, synchronization, and concept accuracy because it provides clear, timed explanatory content deriving the correct image distance and magnification; and more polished in layout and typography. Lesson 1 lacked assessable narration, timing, and interactivity evidence, and was weaker visually and compositionally. The unanimous, high-confidence verdicts indicate a clear overall win for Lesson 2.
